mainTopic: Who pays for city needs: exemptions for תלמידי חכמים, charges on orphans, and how long until one counts as a resident
overview: This amud is about who must pay for city needs, and why תלמידי חכמים are often exempt. It finishes רבי יוחנן's reading of 'I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers' and explains why ריש לקיש reads it like רבא. רב נחמן בר יצחק objects to taxing the רבנן and brings proofs from the תורה, the נביאים and the כתובים. Then come rules about city costs: orphans pay for a new well (with their money returned if it fails), everyone pays for gates except the רבנן, and even the רבנן pay for wells but do not join the digging. The story of רבי's storehouses and the humble רבי יונתן בן עמרם leads to רבי's view that troubles come because of עמי הארץ, shown by the crown tax in טבריא. The גמרא then goes back to the משנה's twelve months: רבא tells apart 'members' and 'residents' of a city, and רבי יוחנן limits the twelve months to paying for the city's protection. The general rule is that even orphans pay for anything that benefits them. The amud ends with stories about charity and orphans, and אביי's answer about the 'great מצוה' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The towers are the Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's reading: 'my breasts are like towers' refers to תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [And 'my breasts are like towers':] these are the Torah scholars.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last piece of a derivation that started just before this point. The towers in the פסוק are the תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full reading is: 'I am a wall' is the תורה, and 'my breasts are like towers' are the תלמידי חכמים. Scholars are already strong like towers because of their תורה, so they do not need the city wall to protect them. That is why they do not have to pay for it.

phrases.english: these are Torah scholars.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the 'towers' from the פסוק quoted just before this point (שיר השירים 8:10).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's derivation, which began before this part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'towers' are Torah scholars, who are protected by their Torah and so need no wall.

steps.title: Why ריש לקיש reads the verse differently
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש did not use this פסוק because he reads it the way רבא does: the wall is כנסת ישראל and the towers are the shuls and study halls.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש holds like רבא's teaching: 'I am a wall' is the Jewish people, and 'my breasts are like towers' are the synagogues and study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש brought a different source and not this פסוק. He understands the פסוק as talking about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a hidden question here: why didn't ריש לקיש use רבי יוחנן's clear פסוק? The answer is that for him (like רבא) the towers are buildings, the בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות, and not scholars. So the פסוק proves nothing about scholars and the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: the community of the Jewish people

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish,
holds in accordance with what Rava expounded:
"I am a wall" – this is the Congregation of Israel,
"and my breasts are like towers" –
these are the synagogues and study halls.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, סָבַר לַהּ כִּדְדָרֵשׁ רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the other אמורא did not use the פסוק from step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone should agree that this פסוק proves scholars need no wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש reads the towers as shuls and study halls, so the פסוק is not about scholars for him.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: towers = תלמידי חכמים. ריש לקיש (like רבא): towers = בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

steps.title: Taxing the Sages is challenged
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא put the poll tax on the רבנן. רב נחמן בר יצחק told him he went against the תורה, the נביאים and the כתובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא placed the head tax on the רבנן. רב נחמן בר יצחק said to him: You have gone against the תורה, the נביאים and the כתובים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a scholar who made other scholars pay a tax. Another scholar strongly objects, and this sets up three proofs that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the topic before it: are scholars exempt from community payments? רב נחמן בר יצחק's attack is very strong. He claims all three parts of תנ"ך exempt scholars. The next steps bring the proofs one by one.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda
imposed the poll tax on the Sages.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to him:
You have transgressed the Torah
and the Prophets and the Writings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme: scholars are exempt from community payments.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's decision to tax the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All three parts of תנ"ך show that Torah scholars are exempt from such taxes.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named רב נחמן here. בר רב חסדא made the tax. בר יצחק objected to it.

steps.title: Proof from the Torah: His holy ones are in God's hand
steps.stepSummary: From דברים: משה asked that even when ה׳ lets the nations rule, His holy ones stay only in His hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the תורה, as it is written: 'Even when He loves the peoples, all His holy ones are in Your hand.' משה said to ה׳: Master of the world, even when You favor the nations, let all Your holy ones be in Your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first of the three proofs. It comes from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה is praying that the nations may rule over Israel, but the 'holy ones' should stay under ה׳'s control alone. If they are not under the rulers' control, they should not pay the rulers' taxes. The next step shows that the 'holy ones' are the scholars.

phrases.english: The Torah – as it is written:
"Even when He loves the peoples,
phrases.notes: דברים 33:3

phrases.english: all His holy ones are in Your hand" –

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Moses said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
even at the time when You hold the nations dear –
phrases.notes: He means: when You let other nations rule over Israel.

phrases.english: let all His holy ones be in Your hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first part of רב נחמן בר יצחק's objection (the תורה).
steps.raayaObject: Torah scholars are exempt from the nations' taxes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 33:3: the holy ones stay in ה׳'s hand, not the rulers'.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the holy ones are the traveling scholars
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reads the rest of the פסוק as describing תלמידי חכמים, who wear out their feet traveling to learn and who discuss ה׳'s words.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they sit at Your feet': רב יוסף taught, these are Torah scholars who wear out their feet going from city to city and country to country to learn Torah. 'Receiving Your words': to discuss the words of ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same פסוק to show that the 'holy ones' are Torah scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף connects the word תֻּכּוּ to מכתתים, 'pounding' the feet. The picture is of scholars who travel far to learn. 'יִשָּׂא מִדַּבְּרוֹתֶיךָ' means they discuss ה׳'s words. So the 'holy ones' who must stay free of the rulers are the scholars.

keyTerms.meaning: they sat / they were crushed (read as pounding their feet)
they wear out their feet (by traveling)

phrases.english: "And they sit at Your feet" –
Rav Yosef teaches:
these are Torah scholars,
who pound their feet
from city to city and from country to country
to study Torah,
"receiving Your words" –
to discuss the utterances of God.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the תורה proof by showing that the 'holy ones' are Torah scholars.
steps.raayaObject: The 'holy ones' in the פסוק are תלמידי חכמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's reading of the end of דברים 33:3.

steps.title: Proof from the Prophets: עולא's Aramaic reading
steps.stepSummary: From הושע: עולא reads יִתְנוּ in Aramaic as 'learn.' If all Israel learns, ה׳ gathers them now. If a few learn, those few are freed from the burden of kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the נביאים, as it is written: 'Though they hire among the nations, now I will gather them, and a few will be released from the burden of king and princes.' עולא said: this פסוק is said in Aramaic. If all of them learn, 'now I will gather them.' If a few of them learn, 'they will be released from the burden of king and princes.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second proof, from the נביאים. עולא reads one word in its Aramaic meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Hebrew, יִתְנוּ seems to mean 'hire.' In Aramaic, תָּנוּ means 'learn' or 'study.' Read this way, even a few who learn Torah are freed from 'the burden of king and princes', which means royal taxes. So scholars should not be taxed.

keyTerms.meaning: the burden of king and princes (taxes)

phrases.english: The Prophets – as it is written:
"Though they have hired among the nations,
phrases.notes: הושע 8:10

phrases.english: now I will gather them,
and they will begin to be diminished a little
from the burden of king and princes" –
Ulla said:
This verse is stated in the Aramaic language:
phrases.notes: He means the word יִתְנוּ, which in Aramaic means 'learn.'

phrases.english: "If they learn" – all of them –
"now I will gather them,"
and if "a few" of them –
"they will be released from the burden of king and princes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second of the three proofs. The proof from the כתובים comes next on the daf.
steps.raayaObject: Those who learn Torah are exempt from royal taxes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 8:10, read with עולא's Aramaic meaning of יִתְנוּ.
steps.whatToRemember: Two of the three proofs so far. תורה: the holy ones (scholars) stay in ה׳'s hand. נביאים: even a few who learn are freed from the king's burden.
steps.whyThisMatters: These proofs stand behind the halacha that תלמידי חכמים are exempt from certain community taxes.

steps.title: The proof from the Writings: no royal taxes on them
steps.stepSummary: The third proof against רב נחמן בר רב חסדא comes from עזרא: it is forbidden to put tribute, impost or toll on those who serve ה׳‎. רב יהודה explains that the three words are three kinds of tax, and one of them is the poll tax itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you went against the כתובים, as it says: 'Tribute, impost, or toll, it is not permitted to put upon them.' רב יהודה said: 'Tribute' is the king's portion, 'impost' is the poll tax, and 'toll' is the ארנונא tax.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last of the three proofs that רב נחמן בר יצחק promised: one from the תורה, one from the נביאים, and now one from the כתובים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in עזרא frees those who serve ה׳ from three kinds of tax. רב יהודה shows that one of them, בלו, is כסף גולגלתא, the very poll tax רב נחמן בר רב חסדא put on the רבנן. So the כתובים openly forbid what he did.

keyTerms.meaning: The Writings, the third part of תנ״ך
The king's portion, a tax paid to the king
Head tax (poll tax), a set amount each person pays
A tax paid with goods or property, collected from time to time

steps.whatToRemember: The three proofs (תורה, נביאים, כתובים) all teach that תלמידי חכמים are not charged the poll tax and other royal taxes.

phrases.english: [And you went against] the Writings —
phrases.notes: This finishes the list from step 3: the תורה, the נביאים, and now the כתובים.

phrases.english: as it is written:
'Tribute, impost, or toll,'
phrases.notes: עזרא 7:24

phrases.english: 'it is not permitted to impose upon them.'
And Rav Yehuda said:
'Tribute' — this is the king's portion,
'Impost' — this is the head tax,
'Toll' — this is the arnona tax.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-part proof that began in step 3, after the תורה (step 4) and נביאים (step 6) proofs.
steps.raayaObject: That רב נחמן בר רב חסדא was wrong to put the poll tax on the רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא 7:24, read by רב יהודה so that בלו means the poll tax.

steps.title: רב פפא charges orphans for a new well
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא made orphans pay their share toward digging a new well. רב שישא בריה דרב אידי objected: maybe no water will come, and the orphans' money will be wasted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא put the cost of digging a new well on orphans too. רב שישא son of רב אידי said to him: But maybe no water will be drawn!
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts: who pays town costs. רב שישא challenges רב פפא for taking money from orphans for a project that might fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grown-up townspeople can agree to risk their money, but orphans cannot agree to give up what is theirs. So if the well turns out dry, the orphans have lost money with no benefit, and that seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Digging a new well or cistern
Water is drawn (the well produces water)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa imposed
[the cost of] digging a new cistern on orphans.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said to Rav Pappa:
But maybe no water will be drawn!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא רְמָא כַּרְיָא חַדְתָּא אַיַּתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from taxes on scholars to another question about town costs: charging orphans.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's decision to collect from orphans for a new well.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the well fails, the orphans lose money, and they are not able to agree to take that risk.

steps.title: רב פפא will return the money if the well is dry
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that he is only taking the money for now. If the well gives water, fine. If not, he will give the orphans their money back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am taking it from them; if water is drawn, it is drawn, and if not, I will give it back to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by showing the orphans can never lose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that orphans might lose money for nothing. רב פפא removes the risk: the orphans pay only if the well works, so the money is never wasted on them.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am taking it from them;
if water is drawn — it is drawn,
and if not — I will give it back to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שישא's challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical fix that removes the risk
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Collecting from orphans could make them lose money if the well fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The money is held on condition: if no water comes, it goes back to the orphans.

steps.title: Everyone pays for city gates, but not the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that everyone must pay for the city gates, even orphans. But the רבנן do not pay, because they do not need that protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Everyone pays for the city gates, even orphans. But the רבנן do not need protection.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a rule about who pays for the town's gates and walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gates protect everyone, so even orphans pay their share. The רבנן are protected by their Torah learning, so they are left out of this cost.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Everyone [pays] for the city gates,
[collecting] even from orphans;
but the Rabbis do not need protection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הַכֹּל לַאֲגַלֵּי גָפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of charging orphans and adds the question of charging the רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, even orphans, pays for city gates; the רבנן are exempt since they need no protection.

steps.title: Everyone pays for wells, but the רבנן do not dig
steps.stepSummary: Everyone, even the רבנן, pays for digging wells, because everyone needs water. But this is only when people give money. If the town goes out together to dig, the רבנן do not go.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone pays for digging wells, even the רבנן. We said this only when people do not go out as a crowd to dig. But if they go out as a crowd, the רבנן are not the kind of people who go out with the crowd.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה's rule continues with wells, and then the גמרא limits it: the רבנן pay money but do not do the physical digging.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike gates, water is something the רבנן need too, so they must pay. But the limit shows the difference between giving money and doing group labor: the רבנן share the cost, not the digging.

keyTerms.meaning: A crowd going out together (to do the work)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules: for gates the רבנן pay nothing, but for wells they do pay; they are only freed from going out to dig.
steps.whatToRemember: Gates: everyone pays except the רבנן. Wells: even the רבנן pay, but they do not join the group labor.

phrases.english: Everyone [pays] for digging cisterns,
[collecting] even from the Rabbis;
And we said this only
when they do not go out as a crowd,
phrases.notes: He means the people just give money and do not dig with their own hands.

phrases.english: but if they go out as a crowd —

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן לָאו בְּנֵי מִיפָּק בְּכָלוֹזָא נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: the Rabbis are not ones to go out with the crowd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רב יהודה's statement, plus a limit on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן pay toward wells, but are free from the group labor of digging.

steps.title: רבי opens his storehouses only to those who learn
steps.stepSummary: In years of drought, רבי opened his storehouses but let in only people who had learned Torah, and not עמי הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי opened his storehouses in years of drought. He said: Let in those who know מקרא, משנה, תלמוד, הלכה and אגדה, but עמי הארץ should not come in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that shows the special treatment given to Torah learners, and sets up the meeting with רבי יונתן בן עמרם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the רבנן get special tax rules, רבי gave food first to those who learned Torah. The list covers every level of learning, from מקרא up to הלכה and אגדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Masters of Scripture, people who learned תנ״ך
Ignorant people who did not learn Torah

phrases.english: Rebbi opened storehouses
phrases.notes: "רבי" alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: in years of drought, he said:
Let masters of Scripture enter,
masters of Mishnah, masters of Talmud,
masters of halachah, masters of aggadah;
but ignorant people should not enter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from tax rules to a story about special treatment for Torah learners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the famine, רבי fed only people who had learned Torah.

steps.title: רבי asks the stranger if he has learned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן בן עמרם pushed his way in and asked to be fed. רבי asked if he had learned מקרא or משנה, and he said no both times, so רבי asked why he should feed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן בן עמרם pushed in and said: רבי, feed me! רבי said: My son, have you learned מקרא? He said: No. Have you learned משנה? He said: No. If so, on what basis should I feed you?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: a man gets in, and רבי tests him by asking what he has learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי is applying his own rule from step 12: food is for those who learned. Since the man answers no to both questions, by that rule he has no claim to be fed.

phrases.aramaic: דָּחַק רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עַמְרָם וְנִכְנַס.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Amram pushed and entered.
He said to him: 'Rebbi, feed me!'
He said to him: 'My son, have you learned Scripture?'
He said to him: 'No.'
'Have you learned Mishnah?' He said to him: 'No.'
'If so, on what basis should I feed you?'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּחַק רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עַמְרָם וְנִכְנַס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by testing רבי's rule on one person.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the man has learned מקרא or משנה, which would give him the right to be fed.

steps.title: Feed me like a dog and a raven
steps.stepSummary: The man asks to be fed the way even a dog and a raven are fed, without having learned anything. רבי feeds him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Feed me like a dog and like a raven. And רבי fed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The man answers רבי's question, and רבי gives him food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer is that even animals who learn nothing still get food, so a person should not be turned away. רבי accepts this and feeds him, so the man gets food even though he claimed no learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dog and like a raven

phrases.english: He said to him: 'Feed me like a dog and like a raven.'
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording. A dog and a raven get food without learning anything.

phrases.english: He fed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question from step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Feed me the way even a dog and a raven are fed, without any learning; רבי then feeds him.

steps.title: רבי regrets feeding the stranger
steps.stepSummary: After the man leaves, רבי sits in distress and regrets giving his bread to an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he left, רבי sat and was upset, and said: Woe is me, that I gave my bread to an ignorant person!
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. רבי feels bad that he fed someone who, as far as he knows, never learned Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's policy was to feed only people who had learned Torah. He gave in to the man's plea, and now he feels he broke his own rule. This sets up the surprise in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: an ignorant person who has not learned Torah

steps.confusionAlert: In this story, plain "רבי" means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: After he left
Rabbi sat and was distressed,
and said: Woe is me
that I gave my bread to an ignoramus!

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר דִּנְפַק יְתֵיב רַבִּי וְקָא מִצְטַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after רבי fed the man.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי regrets breaking his policy of feeding only people who learned Torah.

steps.title: רבי's son suggests it was a humble student
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר רבי suggests the man was really רבי's student יונתן בן עמרם, who never wanted to benefit from his Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון, the son of רבי, said to him: Maybe that was your student יונתן בן עמרם, who never in his life wanted to get benefits from the honor of Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's son offers another way to see what happened: the man was not ignorant at all, just humble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This changes the whole story. The man said he had not learned so that he would not get food as a reward for his Torah. So רבי did not really feed an עם הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: to get benefit from the honor given to Torah

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, said before him:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עַמְרָם תַּלְמִידְךָ הוּא,
phrases.english: Perhaps it was your student Yonatan ben Amram,
who does not want to benefit
from the honor of Torah all his days?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's distress by suggesting the man was really a תלמיד חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man may have been a humble scholar who hid his learning.

steps.title: The guess is confirmed, and רבי lets everyone in
steps.stepSummary: They check and find that it really was יונתן בן עמרם, so רבי orders that everyone may come in.
steps.simpleTranslation: They looked into it and found that it was so. רבי said: Let everyone come in.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. Since even a real scholar might hide his learning, רבי opens the storehouses to all people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי learns that he cannot always tell who has learned Torah. So he drops his rule of letting in only people who learned, and lets everyone in.

keyTerms.meaning: and found it to be so

steps.whatToRemember: רבי first fed only people who had learned Torah. After the story of יונתן בן עמרם, he let everyone in.

phrases.english: They checked and found it was so.
Rabbi said: Let everyone enter.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּדְקוּ וְאַשְׁכַּח. אָמַר רַבִּי: יִכָּנְסוּ הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the son's suggestion and ends the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי opened his storehouses to everyone.

steps.title: רבי's view: suffering comes because of the ignorant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי's first policy fits his own view that punishment comes to the world only because of עמי הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי follows his own way of thinking here, for רבי said: Punishment comes to the world only because of ignorant people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back from the story. It explains why רבי first wanted to keep עמי הארץ out: it fits a view he holds elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "רבי לטעמיה" means this policy is not random. It matches רבי's general belief that hard times come because of עמי הארץ. The next steps bring a story to show this belief.

keyTerms.meaning: following his own reasoning (as he holds elsewhere)

phrases.english: Rabbi follows his own reasoning,
for Rabbi said:
Punishment does not come to the world
except because of ignoramuses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי's first policy of keeping out עמי הארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Punishment comes to the world only because of עמי הארץ.

steps.title: The crown tax in טבריא, first round
steps.stepSummary: A crown tax was put on טבריא. The people asked that the רבנן pay too. רבי refused, half the people ran away, and the government took away half the tax.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like that crown tax that was put on טבריא. The people came to רבי and said: Let the Rabbis pay with us. He said: No. They said: Then we will run away. He said: Run away. Half of them ran away, and the government took away half the tax.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that shows רבי's view. When the עמי הארץ left, the tax went down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The townspeople tried to pressure רבי into making the רבנן pay. He refused, so half of them fled. The tax was cut by half, which hints that the burden was there because of them.

keyTerms.meaning: crown tax, a tax the government puts on a city

phrases.english: Like that crown tax money
phrases.notes: כלילא is a tax the government put on the whole city.

phrases.english: that they imposed on Tiberias,
they came before Rabbi and said to him:
"Let the Rabbis give together with us."
He said to them: "No."
They said to him: "We will run away."
He said to them: "Run away."
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Half of them ran away,
and they lifted off half.
phrases.notes: The government took away half of the tax.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story to support רבי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's view that punishment comes because of עמי הארץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the crown tax in טבריא

steps.title: Second round: everyone flees and the tax disappears
steps.stepSummary: The other half asks the same thing and gets the same answer. They all run away until only a launderer is left. Then he runs too, and the tax is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other half came to רבי and said: Let the Rabbis pay with us. He said: No. They said: We will run away. He said: Run away. They all ran away, and only one launderer was left. The tax was put on the launderer. The launderer ran away, and the crown tax was cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. Each time the עמי הארץ leave, the tax shrinks, until it is gone completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When only the רבנן were left in the city, there was no tax at all. This shows that the tax trouble was connected to the עמי הארץ, not to the רבנן.

phrases.english: That remaining half came before Rabbi,
they said to him: "Let the Rabbis give together with us."
He said to them: "No."
"We will run away." "Run away."
phrases.notes: The townspeople say the first word, and רבי answers with the second.

phrases.english: They all ran away, and one launderer was left.
They imposed it on the launderer.
The launderer ran away, and the crown tax was cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the crown tax story.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's view that punishment comes because of עמי הארץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: Once all the non-scholars left, the tax was cancelled completely.

steps.title: רבי draws the lesson from the story
steps.stepSummary: רבי says: You see, punishment comes to the world only because of עמי הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: You see that punishment comes to the world only because of ignorant people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי points to the story as proof of his view, and the section closes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tax vanished once the עמי הארץ were gone. This ties the story back to the statement in Step 18. It also explains why רבי first fed only people who had learned Torah.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי holds that hard times come because of עמי הארץ. The crown tax in טבריא disappeared once they left, and that view explains his first storehouse policy.

phrases.english: Rabbi said: You have seen
that punishment does not come to the world
except because of ignoramuses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: רְאִיתֶם שֶׁאֵין פּוּרְעָנוּת בָּא לָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the crown tax story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Punishment comes to the world only because of עמי הארץ.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: how long until one counts as a resident
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that asks how long a person must live in a city to count like its people. The answer there is twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long must a person be in the city to be like the people of the city, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. It is setting up a contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that one becomes a full resident, who must pay into city funds, after twelve months. The גמרא quotes this so it can compare it with another source.

keyTerms.meaning: "and so on" (the rest of the quote is left out)

phrases.english: And how long must one be in the city
to be like the people of the city, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה's answer, left out here with "etc.", is twelve months.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה יְהֵא בָּעִיר וִיהֵא כְּאַנְשֵׁי הָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories behind and goes back to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person counts as a resident of a city after twelve months.

steps.title: A contradiction from the caravan in an idolatrous city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a caravan that stayed in an עיר הנדחת and joined the idol worship. Its members get סקילה like individuals, and their property is not destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we raise a contradiction: A donkey caravan or a camel caravan passing from place to place stayed overnight in the city and was led astray with them. They get stoning, and their property escapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a contradiction to the משנה's twelve-month rule. This step brings the beginning of a ברייתא about עיר הנדחת, and the full tension shows up as the ברייתא continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real residents of an עיר הנדחת are killed by the sword and their property is destroyed. Caravan members who only passed through are judged as single idol worshippers with סקילה, and they keep their property. So the ברייתא also has its own measure of who counts as a resident, and the גמרא is setting it against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: and we raise a contradiction against it
a donkey caravan and a camel caravan
was led astray (to worship idols), as in עיר הנדחת
stoning, the death penalty for a single idol worshipper

steps.confusionAlert: Being stoned here is the "lighter" result for property: individuals keep their property, while true residents of an עיר הנדחת get the sword and lose their property.

phrases.english: And we raise a contradiction:
A donkey caravan or a camel caravan
passing from place to place,
and it stayed overnight inside it and was led astray with them,
phrases.notes: "Inside it" means inside a city that went after idol worship (עיר הנדחת).

phrases.english: they are punished by stoning,
and their property escapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a ברייתא against the משנה's twelve-month rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that one becomes a resident of a city after twelve months.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא about the caravan in an עיר הנדחת has its own standard for who counts as a resident, and the גמרא sets it against the משנה's twelve months.

steps.title: Thirty days makes the caravan part of the city
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the caravan stayed thirty days, they are judged like the city's people, with death by the sword and their property destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they stayed there thirty days, they are killed by the sword, and their property is destroyed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא from the last step. This last line is the real punch of the challenge: thirty days already makes someone one of the city's people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before thirty days, the caravan members are judged as individuals, with סקילה and their property saved. After thirty days, they are treated like full townspeople of the עיר הנדחת. So the ברייתא says thirty days is enough, while our משנה says twelve months.

keyTerms.meaning: the sword, the death penalty for the people of an עיר הנדחת

phrases.english: And if they stayed there thirty days
they are killed by the sword, and their property is destroyed!
phrases.notes: This is the punishment for the townspeople of an עיר הנדחת. So after thirty days, the caravan counts as townspeople.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 23, giving the line that actually clashes with the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that twelve months is needed to count as one of the city's people (step 22).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats someone as a townsperson after only thirty days, which seems to contradict the twelve-month requirement.

steps.title: Members of the city versus residents of the city
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that twelve months is for full 'members of the city,' and thirty days is for 'residents of the city.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is not difficult. This one is about the members of the city, and that one is about the residents of the city.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the clash by saying the two sources are talking about two different levels of belonging to a city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a full 'member' (בני מתא) takes twelve months, and that is what the משנה means. Being a 'resident' (יתובי מתא) takes only thirty days, and that is enough for the עיר הנדחת law. So both sources are true, each about its own level.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult; there is no contradiction
members of the city, full townspeople
residents of the city, people living there

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'members' and 'residents' are just two words for the same thing. רבא's whole answer depends on them being two different levels with two different time limits.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult:
This is for the members of the city,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה's twelve months.

phrases.english: that is for the residents of the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 23-24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two categories (two levels of belonging to a city)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought there is only one standard for counting as part of a city, so twelve months and thirty days clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two standards: twelve months for 'members,' thirty days for 'residents.'

steps.title: Proof from a vow about the people of a city
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about vows shows the same two levels: twelve months for 'people of the city' and thirty days for 'residents of the city.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Someone who vowed not to benefit from the people of a city may not benefit from anyone who stayed there twelve months; less than that is allowed. If he vowed not to benefit from the residents of a city, he may not benefit from anyone who stayed there thirty days; less than that is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's two-level answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses two different wordings in a vow and gives each its own time. 'People of the city' means those there twelve months. 'Residents of the city' means those there thirty days. This shows the two levels are real and recognized.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
someone forbidden by a vow to get benefit

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who is forbidden by a vow from benefiting from the people of the city —

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּהָא שָׁם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ –
phrases.english: anyone who stayed there twelve months —
he is forbidden to benefit from him;
less than that — it is allowed.
From the residents of the city —
phrases.notes: Supply the words 'if he vowed not to benefit' from the first case.

phrases.english: anyone who stayed there thirty days —
he is forbidden to benefit from him;
less than that — he is allowed to benefit from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer in step 25 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's distinction between 'members' (twelve months) and 'residents' (thirty days).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about vows forbidding benefit from the people or residents of a city.
steps.whatToRemember: Twelve months makes you a full member of a city. Thirty days makes you a resident.

steps.title: Different times for different city charity funds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether twelve months is needed for everything, since a ברייתא gives shorter times for different charity funds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really need twelve months for everything? But it was taught: thirty days for the food plate, three months for the charity box, six for clothing, nine for burial, twelve for the city's protection!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה again. A ברייתא gives several different time limits for paying into different city funds, and only one of them is twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה sounds like twelve months is the one rule for joining a city's obligations. But this ברייתא shows that some obligations start much sooner, after thirty days, three months, and so on. So twelve months cannot be a rule for every matter.

keyTerms.meaning: the charity food plate, food handed out daily to the poor
the charity box, money collected for the poor
the city's protection, such as its walls and defenses

phrases.aramaic: וּלְכׇל מִילֵּי מִי בָּעִינַן שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ?
phrases.english: And for all matters do we need twelve months?
But wasn't it taught: thirty days — for the food plate;
three months — for the charity box;
six — for clothing;
nine — for burial;
twelve — for the city's protection!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְכׇל מִילֵּי מִי בָּעִינַן שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the משנה's twelve months after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's twelve-month rule, as if it applies to every city obligation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows most city funds must be paid much sooner than twelve months, so twelve months cannot be the general rule.

steps.title: The משנה's twelve months is only about protection
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the twelve months in our משנה is only about paying for the city's protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: When our משנה said twelve months, it was talking about the city's protection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers by limiting the משנה's twelve months to one specific obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is in the middle of a discussion about building the city's wall and gates. So its twelve months is about protection only, which matches the last line of the ברייתא. The other funds start earlier, and there is no clash.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין ״שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ״ –
phrases.english: When we also learned 'twelve months' in our Mishnah —
we learned it about the city's protection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה to one matter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's twelve months is a general rule for every city obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The twelve months applies only to paying for the city's protection; other funds start sooner.
steps.whatToRemember: Different city obligations start at different times. The twelve months of our משנה is only for the city's protection.

steps.title: Everyone pays for protection, even orphans, but not רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says everyone, even orphans, must pay for the city's protection, but רבנן do not, since they do not need protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone pays for the city's protection, even orphans. But רבנן do not, because רבנן do not need protection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same teachers about who must pay for the city's protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Orphans are usually protected from many payments, yet here they must pay because the city's protection benefits them too. רבנן are excused because their Torah learning protects them. This repeats the reason רב יהודה gave earlier for the city gates (step 10).

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone pays for the city's protection, even from orphans we collect;
but Torah scholars — no,
since Torah scholars do not need protection.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַכֹּל לְפַסֵּי הָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second teaching about the same topic, protection costs, now about who pays.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, even orphans, pays for the city's protection; Torah scholars are exempt because they do not need protection.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the reason, repeated several times on this amud, why תלמידי חכמים are exempt from paying for the city's defenses: they do not need protection.

steps.title: רב פפא lists the protection costs
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says even orphans pay for the wall, the horseman, and the guard, but רבנן do not need protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: For the wall, the horseman, and the guard, even orphans pay. But רבנן do not need protection.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא spells out exactly which protection costs even orphans must pay for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא gives concrete examples of 'protection': the city wall, a horseman who patrols, and a guard. He agrees that רבנן are excused for the same reason as before.

keyTerms.meaning: a horseman who guards the city
a guard, such as the guard of the city's weapons

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For the wall, for the horseman, and for the guard — even from orphans;
but Torah scholars do not need protection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְשׁוּרָא וּלְפָרָשָׁאה וּלְטֻרְזִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives specific examples of the protection costs mentioned in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even orphans pay for the wall, the horseman, and the guard; Torah scholars are exempt.

steps.title: The rule: orphans pay for whatever benefits them
steps.stepSummary: The general rule is that even orphans pay for anything they get benefit from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule of the matter: anything they get benefit from, even orphans pay for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the topic with one general rule about orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason orphans pay for protection is not special to walls and guards. The real reason is that they benefit from it. So any city expense that helps them is collected from them too.

keyTerms.meaning: the general rule of the matter

phrases.english: The general rule of the matter:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִילְּתָא דְּאִית לְהוּ הֲנָאָה מִינֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: anything that they have benefit from —
even from orphans we collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the specific examples of steps 29-30 into one general rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Orphans must pay for any city expense that benefits them.
steps.whatToRemember: Even orphans pay for anything that benefits them, like city protection. רבנן do not pay for protection, because they do not need it.

steps.title: רבה collects charity from orphans
steps.stepSummary: רבה placed a צדקה obligation on the orphans of the house of בר מריון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה imposed charity on the orphans of the house of בר מריון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: רבה made the orphans of בר מריון give צדקה. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 said יתומים pay for things they themselves benefit from. Giving צדקה to others does not seem to fit that rule, so רבה's action looks surprising.

phrases.english: Rabba imposed charity
on the orphans of the house of bar Maryon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life case that seems to go further than the rule in step 31, since charity gives the orphans no direct benefit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה collected צדקה from the orphans of בר מריון.

steps.title: אביי objects from a teaching that orphans are never charged charity
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה with רב שמואל בר יהודה's ברייתא: we do not set צדקה on יתומים, even for פדיון שבוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But didn't רב שמואל בר יהודה teach that we do not impose charity on orphans, even for redeeming captives?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's action. He quotes a teaching that says orphans must never be charged צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'even for פדיון שבוים.' That means even the most urgent kind of צדקה cannot be taken from יתומים. So surely an ordinary collection like רבה's should not be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] teach? This is the opening of a challenge from a ברייתא.
We do not set or assess an amount

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
but didn't Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda teach:
One does not impose charity on the orphans –
even for redeeming captives!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's action from step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's collecting צדקה from the orphans of בר מריון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even פדיון שבוים, the most urgent צדקה, cannot be imposed on יתומים, then no צדקה may be taken from them.

steps.title: רבה did it to give the orphans standing
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that he collected from them to raise their importance, not to fulfill a charity obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did it to make them important.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why he did it. His goal was to give the orphans honor and standing, not to charge them a real obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה agrees with the ברייתא. Its rule is about charging orphans an actual צדקה obligation. His collection served a different purpose: making the orphans look important by having them give.

keyTerms.meaning: To make them important, to give them standing

steps.whatToRemember: The rule stands: we do not set צדקה on יתומים. רבה's collection was only meant to give them honor.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here רבה is answering אביי.

phrases.english: I did this to make them important.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה was charging the orphans a real צדקה obligation, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only raising their standing, so the ברייתא's rule is not broken.

steps.title: The king's mother sends money for a 'great מצוה'
steps.stepSummary: איפרא הורמיז, mother of King שבור, sent רב יוסף a purse of דינרים and asked that it go to a great מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: איפרא הורמיז, the mother of King שבור, sent a purse of dinars to רב יוסף. She said: Let it be for a great מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story that also connects to the ברייתא about פדיון שבוים. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She attached a condition: the money must go to a 'great מצוה.' She did not say which מצוה that is, so רב יוסף now has to work it out.

phrases.english: Ifra Hormiz, the mother of King Shapur,
sent a purse of dinars
before Rav Yosef,
she said: Let it be for a great מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story connected to the same ברייתא of רב שמואל בר יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gift was given on the condition that it be used for a 'great מצוה.'

steps.title: רב יוסף wonders what a 'great מצוה' is
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף sat and thought about which מצוה counts as 'great.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף sat and thought about it: What is a 'great מצוה'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks himself which מצוה she meant, so he can use the money correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question looking for information, not an attack. רב יוסף needs a source that shows which מצוה is called great.

keyTerms.meaning: Was thinking it over, looking into it

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף וְקָא מְעַיֵּין בַּהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef sat and was considering it,
what is a 'great מצוה'?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף וְקָא מְעַיֵּין בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the condition in step 35 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מצוה counts as a 'great מצוה'

steps.title: אביי begins to answer from the same teaching
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to answer by quoting רב שמואל בר יהודה's ברייתא about not setting צדקה on יתומים, even for פדיון שבוים, and says 'learn from this.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: From what רב שמואל בר יהודה taught, that we do not impose charity on orphans even for redeeming captives, learn from this...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to answer רב יוסף's question by quoting the same ברייתא from step 33. His sentence is not finished yet, so this step sets up his conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'even for פדיון שבוים.' That wording treats פדיון שבוים as the strongest case of צדקה. אביי is about to draw a lesson from that wording.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ברייתא אביי used in step 33 against רבה. Here he uses it for a different purpose: to answer רב יוסף's question.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
From what Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda taught:
One does not impose charity on the orphans
even for redeeming captives,
learn from this
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet. אביי's point is completed at the start of the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the question in step 36, using the ברייתא first quoted in step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer comes from the 'even for פדיון שבוים' wording of the ברייתא. The conclusion continues on the next amud.
